newsitem.title: UK: Deal reached on Barings' shareholder compensation.
newsitem.headline: Deal reached on Barings' shareholder compensation.

text.p: Administrators of the Barings Group said on Monday they have reached agreement in principle with the London-based City Disputes Panel on a compensation offer for thousands of bondholders who lost nearly 275 million pounds ($450.4 million) in the collapse of the British bank.

In a statement, Ernst and Young administrators Nigel Hamilton, Alan Bloom and Maggie Mills said the matter will be taken forward to court hearings over "the coming months." They provided no further details.
Contributors to the settlement include Barclays Plc investment banking arm BZW, ABN-AMRO broking unit Hoare Govett and accountancy firm Coopers and Lybrand.
Those in line for compensation are large life and pension funds such as Legal & General and Scottish Amicable, as well as many elderly investors.

Barings collapsed in February 1995 after trader Nick Leeson ran up losses of 800 million pounds in massive unauthorised dealing. The bank was rescued by Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV.
